transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start time: 09:02 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rosa Alvarez (CTO, EdgePort), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Tina Wu (Cloud Ops)

Summary: quick sync to review marketplace certification checklist, packaging for Azure/GCP marketplaces, and on-prem/VPC deployment requirements. Discussed installer options, KMS/SAML needs, compatibility with ARM nodes, and what artifacts Redwood needs for listing. Agreed on next steps and a hands‑on workshop for the installer.

Topics: marketplace listing packaging, reference architecture for private deployment, certified artifacts, on‑prem installer workshop, compliance (SOC2/ISO), KMS/SAML, networking, GPU compatibility, fallback strategies (hosted -> dedicated -> on‑prem).

Transcript body (timestamps are approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Rosa, Samir, Tina — thanks for making the time. Today we wanted to walk through the certified listing checklist and the on‑prem deployment design so we can unblock the marketplace publishing and your pilot.
[00:18] Rosa Alvarez: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we're evaluating a listing for our edge orchestrator plus integrated inference, and we need the package so our marketplace team can validate. We're targeting both public cloud marketplaces and an on‑prem "image" or installer for customers that can't go to cloud.
[00:33] Liam O'Connor: Hi all. I'll mostly cover the technical packaging and installation choices — containerized installer, operator, and offline install. Also hardware compatibility and recommended kernel/driver versions.
[00:45] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Our main constraints: some customers run on ARM-based servers (Ampere), others have NVIDIA A10s; storage is a mix — NFS and local NVMe. Network policies are strict, and we need to integrate KMS for secrets.
[01:02] Tina Wu: And from ops — must have SSO via SAML, RBAC controls, audit logs, and the ability to route inference workloads to dedicated pools.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Great. Quick note on naming — our public docs sometimes get transcribed as "Red wood" or "Redword" in automated notes, ignore that. We support shipping a marketplace listing that includes packaging options: container images plus Helm chart for managed clouds, and an on‑prem bundle with an offline installer.
[01:30] Rosa Alvarez: For the on‑prem, we need an offline installer because some of our regulated customers are in air‑gapped environments. Does Redwood have a recommended pattern?
[01:38] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we support an offline bundle — tarball with images and an installer script. Two modes: a lightweight operator for k8s installs, and a direct docker-compose style for single‑node footprints. For air‑gapped, we provide a signed bundle and an installation document that covers verification via SHA256.
[01:58] Samir Patel: And what about the KV cache behavior and memory - we heard some runtimes blow up with big seq lengths. How does Redwood runtime handle KV cache across restarts?
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: Good question. Our runtime maintains a persistent KV cache per model session if you opt in; for on‑prem we expose config to size the cache and swap thresholds. In air‑gapped installs you can set cache to local NVMe and cap the live tokens. The cache is not shared across nodes unless you configure a shared NFS or Redis-based backing, but for most low‑latency inference we recommend keeping local.
[02:35] Rosa Alvarez: Okay. For the marketplace listing our compliance team will ask for SOC2 artifacts and a privacy FAQ. Can Redwood provide redacted SOC2 or an attestation?
[02:44] Maya Chen: We can share a SOC2 summary and our third‑party attestation. For private deployments we provide guidance and an enterprise licensing agreement; we'll send the attestation and a compliance packet.
[02:55] Tina Wu: We also need to ensure KMS integration — customers use AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and some use Hashicorp Vault. Does Redwood runtime support multiple KMS backends?
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we have out‑of‑the‑box integrations for AWS KMS and Google KMS; Hashicorp Vault is supported via a plugin. For on‑prem we can provide an operator that talks to Vault or customer‑managed KMS via env var configuration and mTLS. There was an older doc where we called it "KMS adaptors" and the transcript messed the word, but it's adaptor/connector.
[03:28] Samir Patel: Good. Networking — we need to pin down required ports and whether the installer opens anything by default.
[03:35] Liam O'Connor: Installer will open only loopback and the inference port by default. For clustered installs we need etcd or a control plane connection — ports 2379/2380 for etcd or alternatives. We'll produce a network diagram.
[03:50] Rosa Alvarez: Marketplace packaging — what screenshots and telemetry disclosures do you need? Our legal wants to know what usage telemetry Redwood collects on hosted vs on‑prem installs.
[04:02] Maya Chen: For marketplace listing we ask for product screenshots, brief description, and an operations guide. On telemetry: hosted Redwood will have tokenized usage and metrics; on‑prem customers can opt out of telemetry entirely — we ship an enterprise flag. We'll include a telemetry table in the packet.
[04:18] Tina Wu: Example — a customer cannot have any outbound call to Redwood's control plane. Will that break anything?
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: No, full offline mode is supported for inference. However, features like rollout coordination, cloud backups, and centralized analytics require outbound. For zero outbound installs, you lose centralized metrics but the runtime works. We'll note that in the listing as a capability.
[04:45] (crosstalk)
[04:47] Rosa Alvarez: Sorry — do you have a recommended approach for upgrades for air‑gapped nodes?
[04:51] Liam O'Connor: We do a signed bundle and an upgrade runner that verifies signatures and does a rolling restart. For single‑node, we provide safe rollback tags. We will include a matrix of supported upgrade paths in the ref arch doc.
[05:05] Samir Patel: There's also the question of GPU drivers — some customers run older driver stacks. Does Redwood support older CUDA versions or do we require upgrades?
[05:14] Liam O'Connor: We publish a compatibility matrix. For A100 and A10 we recommend CUDA 11.8+, and we have limited support for 11.4 with caveats. For Ampere/ARM (Neoverse) nodes we support an ROCm-ish path via our community plugins, but limited testing. We'll call that out as "community-supported" in the matrix.
[05:38] Maya Chen: I'll have Liam draft a compatibility table for the listing.
[05:41] Samir Patel: Great. Another item — the marketplace certification team asks for a reference architecture diagram showing network flow and data residency. Can you provide a templated diagram?
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we have templated ref archs for three patterns: hosted (Redwood API), dedicated (reserved GPU pool in a customer's VPC), and private (on‑prem). We'll tailor the private one to show air‑gapped, KMS, and data at rest encryption.
[06:08] Rosa Alvarez: About licensing — our procurement wants to know if we can resell Redwood as part of our solution and how revenue split or license looks.
[06:16] Maya Chen: We have an ISV co‑sell program. I'll loop in partnerships after this call. But for the marketplace listing immediate ask, your marketplace team needs the artifacts — screenshots, a 2‑page install guide, and a compliance checklist.
[06:29] Tina Wu: For the 2‑page install guide — can that be a one‑pager plus a manifest?
[06:33] Liam O'Connor: Yes, a quickstart plus manifest works. We'll provide a short sample manifest for k8s and a compressed artifact for the offline bundle.
[06:42] [07:00] Maya Chen: Quick pause — any blockers on our side to produce those artifacts? Liam?
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: Not really. Time to produce: compatibility table and templated diagrams — 2 business days. The signed offline bundle flow needs security review if we include sample keys; we'll avoid that and provide instructions only.
[07:20] Samir Patel: For compliance docs — any NDA or data processing addendum we need to sign before sharing SOC2?
[07:28] Maya Chen: We can share a SOC2 summary without an NDA; for full reports we'd use an NDA or an encrypted S3 share. If you want full audit artifacts we'll coordinate with legal.
[07:40] Rosa Alvarez: Let's plan for summary now and NDA if needed.
[07:43] Tina Wu: Marketplace listing verification sometimes requires us to run a live test. Do you have a sandbox image we can run in our staging to demonstrate install?
[07:53] Liam O'Connor: Yes — we have a sandbox bundle and a demo dataset that runs in 1‑node with a small model. The demo uses quantized weights to keep memory low. It is good for verification runs. We'll provide that artifact in the listing package.
[08:08] Rosa Alvarez: About partner listing categories — our marketplace requires an architecture review with security team. Will someone from Redwood present to their security folks?
[08:18] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We can schedule a 45‑minute security walkthrough. Liam or our security engineer can join.
[08:25] Samir Patel: Great. Also, could you include a short SLA blurb that we can put in the listing? Some customers ask for latency targets for 0.5s p95 on small models.
[08:35] Liam O'Connor: SLA language we can supply; however specific p95 is workload dependent. We'll include sample numbers from our benchmarks and a note that dedicated capacity gives tighter SLOs. For hosted we can show representative p95 numbers per model family.
[08:55] (minor audio glitch at ~09:02)
[09:05] Rosa Alvarez: About billing metadata — marketplace needs a clear callout of metering units. Redwood charges per token or embedding. Does that map cleanly to a listing unit?
[09:16] Maya Chen: We provide a unitization doc. For marketplace you can list as "inference units" and then map to token/embedding behind the scenes; we'll provide sample pricing snippets for the listing.
[09:28] Samir Patel: Competitors — we've done some checks; BigCloudAI seems to require customers to use their control plane which is a blocker for some customers; ModelServeInc is more self‑host but lacks batching optimizations. Any notes to position us?
[09:43] Maya Chen: Positioning: focus on consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private and the cost controls (batching, quantization profiles). We'll include a short competitive playbook for your listing team.
[09:56] Tina Wu: Alright. On the technical nitty‑gritty — what format should the helm charts be? Does Redwood publish charts to artifact registry or do you expect partners to host them?
[10:06] Liam O'Connor: We publish partner charts to our registry on request; partners can also host in their own registry. For marketplace listings we usually ask for a chart reference and the images to be available in a public or partner‑accessible registry. For air‑gapped we'll provide image tarballs.
[10:22] Rosa Alvarez: Regarding log forwarding — can we forward runtime logs to our ELK stack?
[10:29] Liam O'Connor: Yes — runtime logs can be shipped to stdout and a FluentD/Vector config is included. For on‑prem we recommend Vector to forward to your ELK.
[10:38] Samir Patel: A quick question on quantization — some customers want int8 to save memory. Does Redwood runtime auto‑choose quantization or do we bundle quantized models?
[10:47] Liam O'Connor: We recommend bundling quantized variants for the listing demo. The runtime supports dynamic quantization profiles but we typically ship a recommended quantized model for small deployments.
[10:58] Rosa Alvarez: Can we get a short script that spins up a demo with quantized model? That helps marketplace test.
[11:04] Liam O'Connor: Yes — sample run scripts are part of the demo bundle.
[11:09] Maya Chen: I'll recap next steps at the half hour mark — but before that, any security questions?
[11:15] Tina Wu: One more: SCIM for user provisioning, do you support SCIM v2?
[11:20] Liam O'Connor: We support SCIM v2 and SAML SSO; we can provide an example IdP mapping for common providers.
[11:28] Samir Patel: Ok, good.
[11:30] [12:00] (brief pause as attendees check shared doc)
[12:10] Rosa Alvarez: I see a note in the shared doc about a "fallback policy" — how does that work if dedicated capacity is exhausted?
[12:18] Liam O'Connor: We support automated fallback routing — if a dedicated pool is out of capacity we can route requests to a compatible model on hosted or a lower tier in your dedicated cluster. Policies are configurable per‑route. For on‑prem you can configure spillover to local CPU nodes.
[12:36] Maya Chen: For marketplace listing we should document that behavior and include an example policy.
[12:40] Rosa Alvarez: Yes please.
[12:42] Maya Chen: Note to self — include fallback sample.
[12:45] (background typing)
[13:00] Samir Patel: There was a question earlier about testing — do you do load tests as part of certification?
[13:08] Liam O'Connor: We can provide a load test harness you can run in staging. For marketplace validation we typically ask partners to run a smoke test and we run an integration test against the demo.
[13:20] Tina Wu: Great. For the on‑prem installer workshop — what do you want us to prepare?
[13:27] Liam O'Connor: If you can share a staging node with network access or a VM image, we can run through the installer. Ideally provide root access or a temp account. We'll bring a checklist.
[13:41] Rosa Alvarez: Ops is tight on time; maybe a recorded run first and then an interactive workshop.
[13:47] Maya Chen: That works. We'll record the demo and share ahead of the workshop.
[13:52] [14:20] (small echo, then resumes)
[14:30] Samir Patel: Packaging for GCP marketplace — any specific requirements?
[14:36] Liam O'Connor: GCP requires container images in Artifact Registry and a partner listing with a quickstart. We have a checklist for GCP and Azure; we'll attach those checklists.
[14:46] Rosa Alvarez: For Azure, sometimes they want an ARM64‑native image for certain VMs. Do you build images for arm64?
[14:53] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we publish multi‑arch images (amd64 and arm64) for partners. For GPU support on arm64 we need to validate the driver path; we'll mark that as limited support in the compatibility matrix.
[15:08] Samir Patel: On the legal side — do you provide a DPA template partners can present to customers?
[15:15] Maya Chen: We have a standard DPA template; we'll share it. For partnership resale specifics we'll loop in legal and partnerships.
[15:23] Rosa Alvarez: Anything we should avoid in the listing that causes marketplace rejection?
[15:28] Liam O'Connor: Don't include actual private keys, client secrets, or sample creds — marketplaces flag that. Also avoid untested upgrade claims. Keep the description accurate and link to an operations guide.
[15:42] Tina Wu: Okay.
[15:45] [16:10] Maya Chen: Quick check — are we aligned on deliverables and timelines? I'll read them: Redwood sends draft marketplace package (screenshots, 2‑page install, diagrams), compatibility matrix, signed demo bundle, sandbox scripts — due 2026‑08‑21. EdgePort shares infra inventory, KMS contact, and staging access — due 2026-08-20. Workshop scheduled week of 2026‑08‑24. Does that match?
[16:33] Rosa Alvarez: Yes.
[16:34] Samir Patel: Agreed.
[16:35] Tina Wu: Agreed.
[16:36] Maya Chen: Perfect. A couple of clarifying notes I want to capture — telemetry defaults and how we handle API keys in the listing.
[16:45] Liam O'Connor: API keys: for on‑prem we allow customer‑managed keys, and we document the rotation process. Telemetry defaults: opt‑in for on‑prem, opt‑out for hosted? (laugh) — actually hosted has metrics by default but we anonymize, and on‑prem is opt‑out by default. We'll confirm exact wording.
[17:04] (soft laughter)
[17:08] Rosa Alvarez: That wording is important for procurement.
[17:11] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll be precise.
[17:13] Samir Patel: One last technical — the model catalog: can we pin model versions in the installer so an on‑prem customer doesn't accidentally pull a newer model?
[17:22] Liam O'Connor: Yes, customers can pin model versions; the installer can lock to a model bundle or accept a repo URL for updates. We'll document a recommended pattern.
[17:31] Rosa Alvarez: That's useful.
[17:33] [18:00] (brief hold while files are downloaded)
[18:12] Maya Chen: Any more questions before we wrap?
[18:15] Tina Wu: Nothing else on our side.
[18:16] Samir Patel: All good.
[18:18] Rosa Alvarez: No, thanks.
[18:20] Maya Chen: Ok we'll follow up with the materials. Thanks everyone — talk soon.

End of transcript.

References / Shared artifacts mentioned: "draft marketplace checklist" (link placeholder), "compatibility matrix (NVIDIA/Ampere)" (link placeholder), "on‑prem demo bundle (signed)" (link placeholder), "installer workshop consent" (note).

- EdgePort: provide infra inventory, KMS contact, SCIM/SAML mapping, and staging node details by 2026-08-20.
- Schedule on‑prem installer workshop for week of 2026‑08‑24 (owner: Maya).

Notes on transcription: automated transcript had a few mis‑strings ("Red wood", "K V cache" -> KV cache, "adaptor" vs "adapter") and occasional dropped punctuation; attendees flagged these during the call.
